question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the WHO MDT regimen for paucibacillary (PB) leprosy from that for multibacillary (MB) leprosy?

answers.text: PB leprosy uses rifampicin + dapsone for 6 months; MB leprosy adds clofazimine and extends to 12 months.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. PB-MDT: rifampicin 600mg monthly (supervised) + dapsone 100mg daily × 6 months. MB-MDT: adds clofazimine (300mg monthly supervised + 50mg daily) and extends to 12 months to address the higher bacterial load.

answers.text: Both PB and MB leprosy use identical three-drug regimens but for different durations.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PB regimen is two drugs (rifampicin + dapsone); MB regimen is three drugs (rifampicin + dapsone + clofazimine). The drug count differs, not just the duration.

answers.text: MB leprosy requires monotherapy with clofazimine for 24 months to reduce bacterial load.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Monotherapy is never used in leprosy due to high resistance risk — that is the same principle as TB treatment. MB-MDT uses three drugs.

answers.text: PB leprosy treatment duration is longer than MB because paucibacillary disease is harder to eradicate.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: It is the opposite: MB leprosy requires longer treatment (12 months) due to higher bacterial load compared with PB (6 months).

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the WHO MDT Regimens block. PB=2 drugs × 6 months; MB=3 drugs × 12 months — the difference reflects bacterial burden.
Well done. The key distinction is that MB-MDT adds clofazimine (for its bactericidal + anti-inflammatory properties) and treats for twice as long.
